evidence: simulated: islets placed at published densities, not imaged

endocrineFraction.source: Hahn M, et al. 3D imaging of human organs with micrometer resolution - applied to the endocrine pancreas. Commun Biol 2021;4:1063. doi:10.1038/s42003-021-02589-x
endocrineFraction.note: Islets are about 1-2% of the pancreas; the middle of that range.

isletDiameterUm.source: Hahn M, et al. 3D imaging of human organs with micrometer resolution - applied to the endocrine pancreas. Commun Biol 2021;4:1063. doi:10.1038/s42003-021-02589-x
isletDiameterUm.note: Mean 3D diameter. The count uses the volume of an islet of this diameter, which overestimates the count a little because islet sizes are skewed.

regionalDensity.source: Wang X, et al. Regional differences in islet distribution in the human pancreas--preferential beta-cell loss in the head region in patients with type 2 diabetes. PLoS One 2013;8(6):e67454. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0067454
regionalDensity.note: Similar in head and body, more than 2-fold higher in the tail; 2.0 is the low end. Neck and uncinate are not reported and are taken as head and body.

clusterShare.source: Hahn M, et al. 3D imaging of human organs with micrometer resolution - applied to the endocrine pancreas. Commun Biol 2021;4:1063. doi:10.1038/s42003-021-02589-x
clusterShare.note: About 40% of islets lay in high islet density regions in non-diabetic tissue.

clusterDensityFactor.source: Hahn M, et al. 3D imaging of human organs with micrometer resolution - applied to the endocrine pancreas. Commun Biol 2021;4:1063. doi:10.1038/s42003-021-02589-x
clusterDensityFactor.note: Islet count in high islet density regions about three times the average.

clusterIslets.note: Hahn et al. define a cluster as more than 100 islets; the upper bound and the even spread between are assumptions.

peripheryMm.note: Clusters lie "in the periphery of the gland" (Hahn); their centres are put within this depth of the surface, an assumption.

references.organVolumeNote: Voxels of 0.5 mm, surface voxels counted half. Hahn et al. give an average human pancreas of about 73 cm3.
